opening.argument: The presentation asks viewers to purchase BitClub Network mining pools for $500, $1,000, or $2,000 and ties those purchases to recurring returns, stating that “out of all of them you also get a daily profit share.” It further promotes payment for recruiting others through a referral program, including the claim that viewers can “get paid for anyone you share the Bitcoin club opportunity with.” The offer is presented as continuing mining supported by reinvestment, while the speaker characterizes the returns as daily profits from a shared pool. Although the speaker denies that it is a Ponzi scheme, saying “we have got equipment that we are using and we get paid daily from this equipment,” that denial accompanies the paid pool and referral structure rather than removing those features. Together, these observable claims establish a paid mining opportunity marketed through daily profit sharing and recruitment incentives.
